bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer at src/pcre2_match.c:277:32 while matching the staged one-byte PoC 0x26 ('&'). LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput seeds rand from that byte and derives the initial compile_options from it; because '&' contains no explicit (?C...) callout syntax but the saved stack reaches do_callout, the crashing compile pass must have enabled PCRE2_AUTO_CALLOUT. parse_regex and manage_callouts therefore create META_CALLOUT_NUMBER metadata for the lone literal, and compile_regex emits an OP_CALLOUT item. After compilation succeeds, the harness calls pcre2_set_callout(), pcre2_set_callout stores the callback in mcontext, and match() copies mcontext->callout and mcontext->callout_data into mb->callout and mb->callout_data. That makes do_callout skip its NULL-callback return and evaluate cb.offset_vector = Fovector - 2. Fovector is the `heapframe.ovector` member, declared as `PCRE2_SIZE ovector[2]`, so the subtraction steps two elements before that declared array to fabricate the legacy callout offset vector and UBSan reports it as index -2 out of bounds for type 'size_t [2]'. The fix rewrites the compatibility logic through a separate `callout_ovector` pointer and removes the direct negative-index form on `Fovector`.

source.description: parse_regex consumes the attacker-controlled '&' as an ordinary pattern item instead of a quantifier and routes it into automatic callout handling.
source.value_from: The staged PoC is exactly one byte 0x26 ('&'). That byte has no explicit callout syntax, so the saved do_callout stack implies the crashing compile pass treated '&' as a normal item while PCRE2_AUTO_CALLOUT was enabled and therefore continued into manage_callouts().
source.note: This is the first project-code statement on the vulnerable path that consumes the witness byte and the derived compile options to create the callout-producing control flow.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: Crash site. do_callout subtracts two elements from Fovector and stores the resulting backwards pointer relative to the declared two-element array in cb.offset_vector.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer_trace.txt and default_crash_trace.txt both identify src/pcre2_match.c:277 in do_callout as the crash location, with summary 'index -2 out of bounds for type size_t [2]'.

root_cause.description: Root cause. do_callout models a legacy extended ovector by stepping two elements back from `Fovector` even though `Fovector` names the declared `heapframe.ovector[2]` array.
root_cause.note: Fovector is the macro alias for `F->ovector`, and `heapframe` declares `PCRE2_SIZE ovector[2]` as its final field. The immediately following vulnerable lines save and restore `Fovector[-2]` and `Fovector[-1]`, so this code is explicitly treating the two preceding `PCRE2_SIZE` slots as synthetic overall-match offsets for callouts. The fixing commit introduces a separate `callout_ovector` pointer and replaces the direct negative-index form on `Fovector`.

tainted_value_origin.description: Harness boundary that deterministically maps the single PoC byte into the compile option word used on the crashing compile pass.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The staged PoC file contains exactly one byte, 0x26 ('&'). Because size is 1, that same byte at data[size/2] seeds rand() and therefore controls compile_options.
tainted_value_origin.note: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput is the unscored boundary, but this is the concrete origin of the witness-specific compile option state consumed by the project parser.

parser_admitted.description: This predicate is the sample-specific parser gate for the lone '&': the character is accepted as an ordinary pattern item rather than rejected or reinterpreted as a quantifier, which is the condition that lets the automatic-callout path run.
parser_admitted.note: The saved crashing run later reaches do_callout(), so the accepted continuation after this predicate executed on the witness input.

fine_trace.note: The one-byte PoC 0x26 ('&') is both the entire pattern and the seed byte at data[size/2]. The harness deterministically derives the initial compile_options from that byte; because the saved crash later reaches do_callout even though '&' has no explicit callout syntax, the crashing compile pass must have PCRE2_AUTO_CALLOUT set in this option word.

Source. The current pattern item is the lone '&', so parse_regex does not treat it as a quantifier. That accepted branch consumes the attacker-controlled byte and routes this item through manage_callouts(), which is the path that can synthesize an automatic callout ahead of it.

With PCRE2_AUTO_CALLOUT set, manage_callouts allocates a four-word metadata record in parsed_pattern, tags it as META_CALLOUT_NUMBER, and records the current item's pattern offset 0. This materializes the accepted '&' item as callout state.

depends_on.via: c != CHAR_ASTERISK && c != CHAR_PLUS && c != CHAR_QUESTION_MARK && (c != CHAR_LEFT_CURLY_BRACKET || (tempptr = ptr, !read_repeat_counts(&tempptr, ptrend, NULL, NULL, &errorcode)))

fine_trace.note: compile_regex lowers the synthetic META_CALLOUT_NUMBER record into an executable OP_CALLOUT item in the compiled pattern. The runtime matching loop therefore dispatches do_callout() before processing the literal '&'.

After compilation succeeds, the harness requests callout support for later matching by passing callout_function and &callout_count into pcre2_set_callout(). Without this request, do_callout would later return immediately on a NULL callback.

pcre2_set_callout stores the non-NULL callback pointer and counter address into the match context. This is the source-level callback state that later has to be transferred into the active match block.
Before the main matching loop runs, match() copies the callback state from mcontext into mb. This is the missing causal link between pcre2_set_callout() and do_callout's later mb->callout check.

When the injected OP_CALLOUT item executes, do_callout checks the copied match-block field. Because step 7 populated mb->callout from the registered callback, this guard is false and execution continues into the compatibility offset_vector setup.

Sink and root cause. Fovector is the macro alias for `F->ovector`, and `heapframe` declares `PCRE2_SIZE ovector[2]` as its final field. This statement forms a pointer two elements before that declared array to mimic the legacy extended ovector layout; the next vulnerable lines then save and restore `Fovector[-2]` and `Fovector[-1]` as those synthetic slots. UBSan reports the backwards step at this exact line as 'index -2 out of bounds for type size_t [2]'.

poc.trigger: The staged PoC is the single byte 0x26 ('&'). In the saved vulnerable run, that byte seeds the harness's compile_options, the crashing compile pass inserts an automatic callout before the lone literal, the harness registers callout_function, and matching reaches do_callout's negative Fovector - 2 compatibility expression.
